mission: 'The Stanford Center for AI Safety leads research, education, and policy to ensure AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and beneficial for humanity.' Its research areas are formal methods, learning & control, transparency, AI governance & policy and human-AI interaction, with a strong emphasis on safety-critical autonomous systems. Co-directed by Clark Barrett, Grace Gao and Mykel Kochenderfer. Founding year approximate.

key_work.plain_summary: Kochenderfer and co-authors' book on how to test and validate safety-critical autonomous systems before deployment.

people.role: Co-Director; associate professor of aeronautics & astronautics

warnings.text: AI is being deployed in safety-critical settings faster than rigorous techniques for guaranteeing its behaviour (center mission).

recommendations.text: Use precise mathematical modelling and formal methods to ensure safety, security and robustness (research areas).
Develop AI governance frameworks with policymakers and industry, including standards and best practices.
Calibrate human trust and keep human oversight mechanisms in human-AI teams.
